text:
anita (People Ops): Quick Q — I'm going on unpaid medical LOA starting 2027-05-10. Can I change my 401(k) deferral midyear? Also have an outstanding 401(k) loan — will payroll repayments pause or get offset/taxed if there are missed payments? Vendor is Oakwood Retirement. Any deadlines?

mike-payroll: You can change your deferral election while employed. Important bit: contributions require taxable wages to withhold from, so if there's no pay we can't deduct. If you submit the election change in Workday before payroll cutoff it'll apply to the next pay period that has wages.

olivia-hr: Also note company match only applies to paid earnings. During unpaid LOA we generally don't make employer contributions unless there's a specific leave-pay arrangement. Vesting schedule unaffected.

sam (Oakwood Retirement): Short vendor note — loan repayments stop when there's no payroll to withhold from. If loan goes into default (plan-specific timing, typically after prolonged missed payments or separation), the plan may offset the outstanding loan balance and treat it as a distribution -> taxable event and 1099-R. If you expect to return within a few months, file LOA docs so we track it; we can often keep the loan open for short LOAs. Email loans@oakwood.com with LOA dates to start a conversation.

anita (People Ops): Got it. Is there any way to "catch up" on missed deferrals once I'm back? And what's the process to explicitly pause/start loan repayments so it doesn't auto-default?

lina-payroll: You can't retroactively take missed deferrals out of paychecks that already happened. You can increase future deferral percent (subject to IRS annual limits) to try to make up some of the lost savings, but it's forward-looking only. For loan repayments we coordinate with Oakwood: submit LOA paperwork to benefits@redwood.com and we'll notify Oakwood to document the pause and proposed restart date — that reduces the risk of an automatic offset.

benefits-bot: Reminder: 401(k) election change cutoff is 17:00 PT two business days before the payroll run. See https://payroll.internal/401k-change for form/details.

sam (Oakwood Retirement): Example email subject we recommend so things route fast:

```
Subject: LOA - Anita K - request pause loan repayments - LOA 2027-05-10 to 2027-08-10
Body: attach LOA approval and expected return date, include last 4 of SSN and loan ID
```

anita (People Ops): Thanks — I'll submit LOA docs to benefits@redwood.com and update Workday today. I'll also email loans@oakwood.com with the subject above. Appreciate the help :pray:

mike-payroll: Ping us after you submit and we'll confirm the cutoff timing for the next pay with you. :thumbsup:

olivia-hr: If you want, we can schedule a quick call with Oakwood to walk through options — lmk.

anita (People Ops): Please — a short call would be great. Thanks everyone! :smile:
